slot.brief: Propose a two-step conversion of an alcohol/alkene to an ether via Williamson synthesis with correct alkyl halide choice.

stem: Which of the following reaction sequences is most suitable for the preparation of *tert*-butyl ethyl ether from 2-methylpropan-2-ol?

verdicts.working: Williamson synthesis requires the bulky alkoxide + primary halide. (A) Na converts t-BuOH to t-BuO⁻Na⁺, which does SN2 on primary CH3CH2Br giving t-Bu-O-Et. (B) gives t-BuBr, and EtO⁻ (strong base) causes E2 with the 3° halide → isobutene. (C) NaOH cannot appreciably deprotonate t-BuOH (pKa ~18 > water 15.7). (D) conc. H2SO4/140 °C with a 3° alcohol gives dehydration and ether mixtures, not the target selectively.

working:
Williamson ether synthesis operates via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism where an alkoxide ion attacks an alkyl halide. To prepare an unsymmetrical ether containing a tertiary alkyl group, the tertiary group must be supplied by the alkoxide, and the primary alkyl group must come from the alkyl halide:

1. Formation of alkoxide:
Aliphatic alcohols are weaker acids than water and cannot be deprotonated by $\text{NaOH}$. An active alkali metal like $\text{Na}$ is used:
$$2(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2\uparrow$$

2. $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ ether synthesis:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$$
Because ethyl bromide is a primary halide, nucleophilic substitution dominates over elimination, giving *tert*-butyl ethyl ether in good yield.

Independent check: Williamson synthesis requires the bulky alkoxide + primary halide. (A) Na converts t-BuOH to t-BuO⁻Na⁺, which does SN2 on primary CH3CH2Br giving t-Bu-O-Et. (B) gives t-BuBr, and EtO⁻ (strong base) causes E2 with the 3° halide → isobutene. (C) NaOH cannot appreciably deprotonate t-BuOH (pKa ~18 > water 15.7). (D) conc. H2SO4/140 °C with a 3° alcohol gives dehydration and ether mixtures, not the target selectively.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option B encodes using a tertiary alkyl halide with an alkoxide base: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-Br} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{ONa}$ undergoes exclusively E2 elimination to yield 2-methylpropene rather than ether.
Option C encodes the misconception that aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ can deprotonate aliphatic alcohols; water is more acidic than *tert*-butanol, so alkoxide formation is negligible and $\text{OH}^-$ simply hydrolyzes the alkyl halide to ethanol.
Option D encodes using acid-catalyzed bimolecular dehydration; tertiary alcohols rapidly undergo unimolecular dehydration to give 2-methylpropene, while any bimolecular condensation of ethanol gives diethyl ether.
